meta.grounding: Synthesized by Claude from the five processed feeds. Every figure traces to primary NYC data; interpretation is the model's and clearly hedged.

headline: Filings run 23% above last year while May 2026 recorded sales fall 15%, with ownership costs requiring 2.25x the citywide median income
summary: July 2026 development filings reached 1,532 citywide (73,798 units), up 23% year over year and 15% above baseline, while May 2026 recorded sales fell to 3,921, down 15% year over year even as the all-property median rose 5% to $940,000. Capital conditions as of August 14, 2026 are mixed: the 10-Year Treasury is 4.68% (+41 bps y/y) and the 30-year mortgage 6.67% (+9 bps), while SOFR at 3.66% and Fed Funds at 3.63% are both roughly 70 bps lower than a year ago. On ACS 5-year 2024 data, buying the citywide median residential home at 6.67% requires $181,150 against a median household income of $80,483 — a 2.25x gap, with 21% estimated able to afford and 52% of renters cost-burdened.

insights.title: Filing and sales signals moved in opposite directions citywide
insights.detail: July 2026 filings totaled 1,532 (+23% y/y, +15% vs. baseline) while May 2026 recorded sales totaled 3,921 (-15% y/y). Manhattan filings rose 57% to 108 and Brooklyn's rose 32% to 491, both flagged Elevated; on the transaction side Queens (-27%, 1,116 sales) and Staten Island (-28%, 249 sales) are flagged Cooling. DATA notes filings are proposed pipeline activity and sales are transaction liquidity, and that filings are not rate-driven.

insights.title: Rates: short end lower, long end higher
insights.detail: As of August 14, 2026: 10-Year Treasury 4.68% (+41 bps y/y), 30-year mortgage 6.67% (+9 bps), SOFR 3.66% (-71 bps), Fed Funds 3.63% (-70 bps). Against the 2021 low-rate boom, the mortgage rate comparison is 2.96% versus 6.36% and recorded sales per month 5,902 versus 4,358, a 26% change. The reported year-over-year correlation between the mortgage rate and sales is -0.21, which DATA labels association, not causation.

insights.title: Ownership gaps are widest in low-income, majority-renter ZIPs
insights.detail: ACS 5-year 2024: 10454 in the Bronx shows a 6.77x affordability gap on a $24,086 median income with 61% of renters cost-burdened; 10029 (Manhattan) 4.75x with 53%; 10030 (Manhattan) 4.37x with 65%; 10453 (Bronx) 4.19x with 65%. These are ownership-cost gaps in majority-renter areas, so the operative pressure shows up in renter cost burden rather than in home purchasing.

insights.title: LL97 exposure concentrates ahead of the 2030 limits
insights.detail: For report year 2024, 28,925 covered buildings were assessed: 18% over the 2024 limit and 73% over the 2030 limit, with estimated annual penalties of $759M (2024) rising to $2,282M (2030). Manhattan accounts for $381M with 75% over the 2030 limit; the Bronx shows 78% over 2030 on $142M.

insights.title: Rising-filing ZIPs co-occur with heavy hazardous-violation counts
insights.detail: In the March–May 2026 cross-signal set, Flatbush-East (11203) pairs 100% filings growth and -18% sales with 973 immediately hazardous violations; Ocean Parkway-North (11218) pairs +144% filings and -26% sales with 495; Bay Ridge (11209) pairs +67% filings and -47% sales with 388. Citywide, 311 complaints reached 186,037 over May–July 2026, up 21% y/y, with $38M in ECB balances.

neighborhoods.narrative: Canarsie appears in both risk and cross-signal feeds: risk pressure of 1,242 with 242 Class C violations, up 61% y/y (May–July 2026), alongside filings up 123% and sales down 25% (March–May 2026) with 219 immediately hazardous violations. Brooklyn borough-wide risk pressure is 86,467 with a Stable trend and 4% y/y change.

Filings rose 78% while recorded sales fell 44% in March–May 2026, with 164 immediately hazardous violations. Brooklyn recorded 1,049 sales in May 2026 at a $1,075,000 all-property median, down 7% y/y and classed In range; borough filings were 491 in July 2026, up 32% and Elevated.

May 2026 sales were 249, down 28% and flagged Cooling, with a $725,000 all-property median, while July 2026 filings rose 30% to 195 (Elevated). On ACS 5-year 2024 figures, Staten Island's affordability gap of 1.51x is the smallest of the five boroughs (Manhattan 2.58x, Bronx 2.58x, Brooklyn 2.56x, Queens 1.74x), with 31% estimated able to afford — though 57% of renters are cost-burdened and the borough is classed Affordability stress. Great Kills (10308) showed sales up 39% with filings down 29% and 11 immediately hazardous violations.

May 2026 sales fell 27% to 1,116 at a $778,500 all-property median (Cooling), while July 2026 filings of 398 were up 9% and In range. ACS 5-year 2024 shows a 1.74x gap, 25% able to afford, and 53% renter cost burden, classed Supported growth. Richmond Hill (11419, +88%), Astoria (11105, +83%), Flushing-South (11365, +77%) and Belle Harbor (11694, +55%) all recorded rising risk pressure in May–July 2026; Jamaica Estates (11432) pairs +128% filings with -30% sales and 379 immediately hazardous violations.

Filings rose 57% to 108 in July 2026 (Elevated); May 2026 sales of 1,184 were down 2% at a $1,440,000 all-property median (In range), and Upper East Side (59-79) (10075) recorded sales up 38% with filings down 50%. Risk pressure of 53,687 is Stable at +10% y/y, though Upper West Side (59-79) (10023) rose 75%, Greenwich Village-West (10014) 106%, and Tribeca (10013) 87%. ACS 5-year 2024 puts the income required to buy at $267,881 against a $103,931 median income, a 2.58x gap, classed Affordability stress.
